docs.title: Home
docs.text:
A Pythonic interface for the Debezium Embedded Engine to stream database Change Data Capture (CDC) events directly in Python — without running Kafka Connect.

Powered by

Get Started Schema Subsystem GitHub

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Schema-Aware Arrow Consumer

    Compile Debezium schemas into Apache Arrow (pyarrow.Schema and pyarrow.Table) with automatic schema tracking and SchemaDiff calculation.

    Schema Subsystem →

  • Multi-Format Embedded Engine

    Configure and run the embedded Debezium Engine using Python dicts or DebeziumConfig in either "json" or Kafka "connect" (SourceRecord) wire formats.

    Configuration Guide →

  • Apache Iceberg Handler

    Stream CDC events directly into Apache Iceberg tables with automatic schema management (IcebergChangeHandlerV2) or raw JSON appends.

    Iceberg Handler →

  • dlt Integration

    Load CDC events into DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, and any other dlt destination using DltChangeHandler.

    dlt Handler →

  • Apache Airflow & Utilities

    Run Debezium engines inside Airflow DAGs via DebeziumEngineOperator, or execute bounded snapshot/timeout runs with Utils.

    Airflow Operator → · Helpers →

  • Bundled Debezium Connectors

    Ships with standard Debezium connectors for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, and Db2 out of the box via JPype.

    How it Works →

docs.title: Quick Start
Apache Airflow Operator
docs.text:
pydbzengine provides built-in integration with Apache Airflow via the DebeziumEngineOperator located in pydbzengine.airflow.

This operator wraps DebeziumEngine to run it as a task in Airflow, handling task execution and proper interruption/shutdown when a task is killed.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
To use the Airflow operator, you must install the dev extra dependencies or have apache-airflow installed:

pip install "pydbzengine[dev] @ git+https://github.com/memiiso/pydbzengine.git"

docs.title: DebeziumEngineOperator
docs.text:
The operator constructor takes a pre-configured DebeziumEngine instance (or DebeziumJsonEngine) and standard Airflow BaseOperator arguments.

class DebeziumEngineOperator(BaseOperator):
    def __init__(self, engine: DebeziumEngine, **kwargs) -> None
  • engine: A configured instance of DebeziumEngine.
  • **kwargs: Pass-through arguments for BaseOperator (e.g. task_id, dag, retries).

When Airflow halts the task, the operator automatically calls engine.interrupt() (via on_kill) to gracefully shut down the Debezium engine and the JVM.

docs.title: Example DAG
docs.text:
Here is an example demonstrating how to run Debezium within a DAG using a custom handler that prints change records:

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import List
from airflow import DAG
from pydbzengine import ChangeEvent, BasePythonChangeHandler, DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.airflow import DebeziumEngineOperator


class MyPrintHandler(BasePythonChangeHandler):
    def handleJsonBatch(self, records: List[ChangeEvent]):
        for record in records:
            print(f"Captured event on table {record.destination()}: {record.value()}")


default_args = {
    "owner": "airflow",
    "start_date": datetime(2026, 1, 1),
    "retries": 1,
    "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=5),
}

with DAG(
    dag_id="debezium_cdc_dag",
    default_args=default_args,
    schedule_interval="@daily",
    catchup=False,
) as dag:
    # Define Debezium configurations
    dbz_properties = {
        "name": "airflow-cdc-engine",
        "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
        "database.hostname": "localhost",
        "database.port": "5432",
        "database.user": "postgres",
        "database.password": "postgres",
        "database.dbname": "postgres",
        "topic.prefix": "airflow_cdc",
        "offset.storage": "org.apache.kafka.connect.storage.FileOffsetBackingStore",
        "offset.storage.file.filename": "/tmp/offsets.dat",
        "snapshot.mode": "initial_only",
        "schema.history.internal": "io.debezium.storage.file.history.FileSchemaHistory",
        "schema.history.internal.file.filename": "/tmp/schema_history.dat",
    }

    # Instantiate engine and handler
    engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=dbz_properties, handler=MyPrintHandler())

    # Create the task
    run_debezium_task = DebeziumEngineOperator(
        task_id="run_debezium_cdc",
        engine=engine,
    )

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: pydbzengine accepts a Python dict[str, Any] whose keys map directly to Debezium's Java configuration properties.

docs.title: Core Engine Properties
docs.text:
Every DebeziumEngine instance requires basic identification and offset storage properties:

Property Description Example name Unique logical name of the engine instance. "engine" connector.class Java class path of the Debezium connector. "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector" offset.storage Storage class used to persist source offsets. "org.apache.kafka.connect.storage.FileOffsetBackingStore" offset.storage.file.filename Local file path where offsets are written. "/path/to/offsets.dat" offset.flush.interval.ms Interval at which offsets are flushed to storage. "1000"

docs.title: Engine Wire Formats
docs.text:
DebeziumEngine supports two record wire formats: - "json" (default): Events are serialized as JSON strings. Schemas are enabled by default (converter.schemas.enable=true), which is required by SchemaAwareChangeHandler. Set converter.schemas.enable=false only when consuming raw schemaless JSON with BasePythonChangeHandler (or built-in handlers such as DltChangeHandler). - "connect": Events are passed as in-memory Java Kafka Connect SourceRecord objects (always schema-enabled).

from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine

# JSON mode (default)
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=dbz_properties, handler=handler)

# Kafka Connect mode
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=dbz_properties, handler=handler, format="connect")

docs.title: Typed Configuration (DebeziumConfig)
docs.text:
You can wrap properties in DebeziumConfig to validate wire format, schema mode, and heartbeat routing up front and share the same immutable config between DebeziumEngine and standalone EventConverter.from_config():

from pydbzengine import DebeziumConfig, DebeziumEngine, EventFormat

config = DebeziumConfig(
    properties=dbz_properties,
    format=EventFormat.JSON,
    schemas_enabled=True,
    heartbeat_prefix="__debezium-heartbeat",
)
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=config, handler=handler)

DebeziumConfig fails fast with ValueError if explicit arguments conflict with keys inside properties (such as converter.schemas.enable, value.converter, or topic.heartbeat.prefix).

docs.title: Schema History Properties
docs.text:
Connectors that track DDL history (MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, Db2) require an internal schema history store:

Property Description Example schema.history.internal Storage class for database schema history. "io.debezium.storage.file.history.FileSchemaHistory" schema.history.internal.file.filename Local file path for storing schema history. "/path/to/schema_history.dat"

docs.title: Database Connection Properties
docs.text:
dbz_properties = {
    "database.hostname": "localhost",
    "database.port": "5432",
    "database.user": "postgres",
    "database.password": "postgres",
    "database.dbname": "postgres",
    "topic.prefix": "cdc_prod",
    "table.include.list": "inventory.customers,inventory.orders",
}

docs.title: Event Unwrapping (ExtractNewRecordState)
docs.text:
By default, Debezium wraps change events in an envelope structure containing before, after, op, source, and timestamp metadata.

  • SchemaAwareChangeHandler compiles whatever top-level struct Debezium emits: without an SMT, schema.arrow_schema and batch.to_arrow() mirror the full envelope (before/after as nested structs).
  • When you want flat table columns directly (for SchemaAwareChangeHandler warehouse sinks, IcebergChangeHandlerV2, or DltChangeHandler), configure Debezium's ExtractNewRecordState transform:
dbz_properties.update(
    {
        "transforms": "unwrap",
        "transforms.unwrap.type": "io.debezium.transforms.ExtractNewRecordState",
        "transforms.unwrap.add.fields": "op,table,source.ts_ms,sourcedb,ts_ms",
        "transforms.unwrap.delete.tombstone.handling.mode": "rewrite",
    }
)

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Fork the Repository: Create a fork of memiiso/pydbzengine on GitHub.
  2. Clone Locally: 
    git clone https://github.com/your-username/pydbzengine.git
cd pydbzengine

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a Branch: Use a descriptive name for your feature or bug fix.
  2. Make Changes: Write your code and tests.

  3. Run Tests:

    To run fast unit tests (no Docker required, ~5 seconds): 

    python -m unittest discover -s tests/unit

    [!IMPORTANT] Docker Prerequisite for Integration Tests: The integration test suite (tests/integration/) uses testcontainers to spin up real PostgreSQL database, Apache Iceberg REST catalog, and MinIO storage instances. Docker must be running on your machine to execute them.

    To run integration tests: 

    python -m unittest discover -s tests/integration

    To run the entire test suite: 

    python -m unittest discover -s tests
    4. Update Documentation: If you're adding a new feature or changing behavior, update the relevant docs/ files. 5. Submit a Pull Request: Push your branch to your fork and create a PR against the main branch.

docs.title: Helper Utilities
docs.text: The pydbzengine library provides a set of helper functions inside the Utils class (located in pydbzengine.helper) to help manage the engine's lifecycle, run the engine asynchronously, or run until snapshots complete.

docs.title: Utils.run_engine_async
docs.text:
Runs the given engine's run method in a separate background thread with a maximum duration (timeout). If the engine exceeds the timeout limit, it logs a warning and calls engine.close().

@staticmethod
def run_engine_async(
    engine: DebeziumEngine, timeout_sec: int = 22, blocking: bool = True
)
  • engine: The DebeziumEngine (or DebeziumJsonEngine) instance to execute.
  • timeout_sec: The maximum execution time in seconds. Defaults to 22.
  • blocking: If True, blocks the calling thread (e.g. main thread) using join() until the engine completes or times out. Defaults to True.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.helper import Utils

# Run the engine for exactly 60 seconds and then stop
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=props, handler=handler)
Utils.run_engine_async(engine=engine, timeout_sec=60)

docs.title: Utils.run_engine_until_snapshot
docs.text:
Runs the Debezium engine in a daemon thread and monitors logging outputs. Once the log message "Snapshot completed" is detected, the engine is shut down gracefully. This is extremely useful for loading initial tables/snapshots when using snapshot.mode = initial_only (or equivalent Debezium snapshot modes) in batched ingestion jobs.

@staticmethod
def run_engine_until_snapshot(engine: DebeziumEngine, poll_interval_sec: int = 1)
  • engine: The DebeziumEngine (or DebeziumJsonEngine) instance to execute.
  • poll_interval_sec: The frequency (in seconds) to check log handlers for snapshot completion. Defaults to 1.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.helper import Utils

# Config properties include: "snapshot.mode": "initial_only"
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=props, handler=handler)
Utils.run_engine_until_snapshot(engine=engine)

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text:
pydbzengine bridges Python applications and the Java-based Debezium Embedded Engine.

Built on Embedded Engine

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: At its core, pydbzengine leverages JPype to: 1. Launch a JVM: A Java Virtual Machine is started within the Python process. 2. Load Debezium Jars: The library bundles the necessary Debezium Engine and connector JAR files. 3. Proxy Objects: It wraps Java objects and types in Pythonic interfaces, allowing you to use Properties and DebeziumEngine as if they were native Python classes (with DebeziumJsonEngine provided as a backward-compatible subclass).

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Configuration: You define your Debezium configuration using a standard Python dictionary or Java Properties.
  2. Engine Initialization: The DebeziumEngine is initialized with these properties, a Python-based handler, and the chosen format ("json" or "connect").
  3. Event Capture: The Java Debezium Engine captures CDC events from your source database.
  4. Batch Processing: Instead of processing events one by one in Java, pydbzengine passes batches of events to your Python handler's handle_batch method (handleJsonBatch is also supported for backward compatibility).
  5. Python Logic: Your custom logic (or built-in handlers like Iceberg/dlt) processes the ChangeEvent objects in pure Python.

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text: By processing events in batches and leveraging Arrow/Parquet internally for handlers like Iceberg, pydbzengine maintains high throughput while providing the flexibility of Python.

docs.title: JVM & Troubleshooting
docs.text: Because pydbzengine operates by running a Java Virtual Machine (JVM) inside the Python process using JPype, you may run into JVM-specific initialization errors. Here is how to resolve them:

docs.title: 1. JVMNotSupportedException or Cannot Locate JVM
docs.text:
If JPype cannot automatically find your Java installation, you will see errors during engine startup.

  • Solution: Ensure that JDK 17 or newer is installed.
  • Environment Variable: Set the JAVA_HOME environment variable pointing to your JDK home directory: 
    # macOS example (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bash_profile)
export JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)

# Linux example
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64

docs.title: 2. JVMAlreadyStartedException
docs.text:
JPype starting restriction means the JVM can only be initialized once per Python process. If another library starts the JVM, or if you run multiple tests that independently initialize JVM setups, JPype will throw a JVM already started warning or error.

  • Solution: The initialization module in pydbzengine.engine.jvm checks jpype.isJVMStarted() before startup (and you can call from pydbzengine.engine.jvm import ensure_jvm_started). However, if you are writing custom JVM startup scripts, always wrap it: 
    import jpype

if not jpype.isJVMStarted():
    jpype.startJVM(...)

docs.title: 3. ClassNotFoundError (Debezium classes not found)
docs.text:
If the Debezium engine fails with Java class definition errors, the .jar dependencies might be missing or corrupted.

  • Solution: Re-run the installation of the package or, if developing locally, execute: 
    ./pydbzengine/install_libs.sh
    This script downloads and copies all required connector jar files from Maven into the library directory pydbzengine/debezium/libs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You must have a Java Development Kit (JDK) version 17 or newer installed and available in your system's PATH.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
Install the latest stable release from PyPI:

# Core engine
pip install pydbzengine

# With optional extras
pip install "pydbzengine[arrow]"    # Required for pydbzengine.schema
pip install "pydbzengine[iceberg]"
pip install "pydbzengine[dlt]"
pip install "pydbzengine[airflow]"

docs.text:

If a recent release is missing from PyPI (for example, due to package size limits on bundled .jar artifacts) or you need unreleased changes from main, you can install directly from GitHub instead.

docs.title: Handlers Overview
docs.text: pydbzengine comes with several built-in handlers to stream CDC events directly into common data destinations. You can also easily create your own by extending the BasePythonChangeHandler.

docs.title: Available Handlers
docs.text:
• Schema-Aware Consumer (SchemaAwareChangeHandler): Base class in pydbzengine.schema (pydbzengine[arrow]) providing compiled PyArrow schemas, SchemaDiff tracking, and homogeneous TableBatch delivery.
  • Apache Iceberg: Stream change events directly into Apache Iceberg tables. Supports automatic schema inference and partitioning (via IcebergChangeHandlerV2).
  • dlt (data load tool): Integrate with dlt to load data into DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, and more.
  • Custom Handlers (BasePythonChangeHandler): Process raw ChangeEvent batches directly in Python (including schemaless JSON).

docs.title: Using a Handler
docs.text:
To use a handler, simply pass an instance of it to the DebeziumEngine:

from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.handlers.iceberg import IcebergChangeHandlerV2

# ... setup catalog and props ...
props = {
    "name": "engine",
    # ...
}
handler = IcebergChangeHandlerV2(catalog=catalog, ...)
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=props, handler=handler)
engine.run()

docs.title: Custom Handlers
docs.text:
Extend BasePythonChangeHandler to process raw ChangeEvent batches directly (including schemaless JSON payloads).

Need typed Arrow tables or schema evolution tracking?

If you consume schema-enabled events and want compiled pyarrow.Schema / pyarrow.Table batches with SchemaDiff tracking, subclass SchemaAwareChangeHandler instead.

docs.title: Creating a Handler
docs.text:
Implement handle_batch(self, records: list[ChangeEvent]) (legacy handleJsonBatch is still supported for backward compatibility):

from pydbzengine import BasePythonChangeHandler, ChangeEvent, DebeziumEngine


class MyCustomHandler(BasePythonChangeHandler):
    def handle_batch(self, records: list[ChangeEvent]) -> int:
        for dest, dest_records in self.group_by_destination(records).items():
            self.logger.info("Processing %d event(s) for %s", len(dest_records), dest)
            for record in dest_records:
                key = record.key()
                value = record.value()
                # Process event (e.g., forward to queue, API, or database)
        return len(records)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=dbz_properties, handler=MyCustomHandler())
    engine.run()

BasePythonChangeHandler also provides:

  • configure(self, config: DebeziumConfig) -> None: Lifecycle hook called automatically by DebeziumEngine at initialization.
  • group_by_destination(self, records: Sequence[ChangeEvent]) -> dict[str, list[ChangeEvent]]: Groups events by destination while preserving arrival order.
  • self.logger: Hierarchical Python logging.Logger instance (from LoggingMixin).

docs.title: The ChangeEvent Object
docs.text:
ChangeEvent mirrors Debezium's ChangeEvent / Kafka ConnectRecord interface:

  • destination() -> str: Destination topic or table name (e.g., inventory.customers).
  • key() -> Any: Record key — JSON string in "json" mode, Java Connect object in "connect" mode, or None for keyless tables.
  • value() -> Any: Record payload — JSON string in "json" mode, Java Connect SourceRecord in "connect" mode, or None for delete tombstones.
  • partition() -> int: Source partition number.

docs.title: dlt (data load tool) Handler
docs.text: The DltChangeHandler integrates seamlessly with the dlt library, allowing you to load CDC events into any destination dlt supports.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Schema Evolution: leverages dlt's powerful schema inference and evolution capabilities.
  • Multi-Destination: Supports DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, and more.
  • Normalization: Automatically normalizes nested data according to your dlt configuration.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
import dlt
from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.handlers.dlt import DltChangeHandler

# Create a dlt pipeline
dlt_pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
    pipeline_name="dbz_cdc_events", destination="duckdb", dataset_name="dbz_data"
)

handler = DltChangeHandler(dlt_pipeline=dlt_pipeline)

# Run with DebeziumEngine
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=dbz_properties, handler=handler)
engine.run()

For a full working example, see dlt_consuming.py.

docs.title: Apache Iceberg Handler
docs.text: The primary Iceberg handler is IcebergChangeHandlerV2. It is designed to stream CDC events directly into Apache Iceberg tables, automatically inferring schemas and managing table structures.

docs.title: IcebergChangeHandlerV2 (Recommended)
docs.text:
This is the most advanced handler, which automatically infers the schema from the Debezium events and creates well-structured Iceberg tables.

  • Automatic Schema Inference: Inspects the first batch of records and infers the schema using PyArrow, preserving native data types (e.g., LongType, TimestampType).
  • Use Case: Ideal for scenarios where you want the pipeline to automatically create tables with native data types that mirror the source.
  • Robustness: If a field's type cannot be inferred (e.g., all null), it safely falls back to StringType.
  • Metadata: Adds _consumed_at, _dbz_event_key, and _dbz_event_key_hash columns for traceability.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
from pyiceberg.catalog import load_catalog
from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.handlers.iceberg import IcebergChangeHandlerV2

conf = {
    "uri": "http://localhost:8181",
    "warehouse": "warehouse",
    "s3.endpoint": "http://localhost:9000",
    "s3.access-key-id": "minioadmin",
    "s3.secret-access-key": "minioadmin",
}
catalog = load_catalog(name="rest", **conf)
handler = IcebergChangeHandlerV2(
    catalog=catalog, destination_namespace=("iceberg", "debezium_cdc_data")
)

# Run with DebeziumEngine
engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=dbz_properties, handler=handler)
engine.run()

docs.title: IcebergChangeHandler (V1)
docs.text:
A simpler handler that appends change data to a source-equivalent Iceberg table using a fixed schema.

  • Structure: The before and after payloads are stored as complete JSON strings.
  • Use Case: Best for creating a "bronze" layer where you want to capture the raw Debezium event exactly as it comes, absorbing all source system schema changes automatically.

docs.title: Schema Subsystem Architecture (pydbzengine.schema)
docs.text:
The pydbzengine.schema package compiles schema-enabled Debezium ChangeEvent batches into Apache Arrow (pyarrow) schemas, tables, and typed Python domain entities.

Downstream consumers that extend SchemaAwareChangeHandler receive compiled TableSchema descriptors, structural SchemaDiff objects, homogeneous TableBatch runs, and ordered lifecycle events rather than raw JSON strings or Java Kafka Connect SourceRecord objects.

Installation & Schema-Enabled Requirement

pydbzengine.schema requires the optional Arrow extra (pip install pydbzengine[arrow]) and schema-enabled events: either EventFormat.CONNECT (format="connect") or EventFormat.JSON (format="json") with schemas_enabled=True (converter.schemas.enable=true, the default). Passing schemaless JSON (schemas_enabled=False) fails fast with a ValueError. If you consume schemaless JSON payloads, subclass BasePythonChangeHandler directly.

docs.title: Raw vs. Schema-Aware Consumption
docs.text: Capability BasePythonChangeHandler SchemaAwareChangeHandler (pydbzengine.schema) Input Contract Raw ChangeEvent strings or Java SourceRecord proxies Typed TableBatch and ChangeRecord entities Supported Modes Connect, schema-enabled JSON, and schemaless JSON Schema-enabled Connect and JSON (schemas_enabled=True) Wire Format Resolution Handled manually by the consumer Resolved once from DebeziumConfig via configure() Type Conversion Raw JSON primitives, Base64 strings, or Java objects Single-pass conversion to Python types and pyarrow.DataType Tabular Output Manual dictionary construction Direct batch.to_arrow(target_schema=...) (pyarrow.Table) Schema Tracking Manual tracking per destination Automatic on_table_created and on_schema_evolved hooks with SchemaDiff Intra-Batch DDL & Lifecycle Mixed schema versions and event kinds in one list Homogeneous TableBatch runs plus composable of_kind(), group_by_kind(), and group_by_destination() sub-batches

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
Import consumer-facing types from pydbzengine.schema:

Category Public Exports (from pydbzengine.schema import ...) Domain Models TableSchema, SchemaDiff, ChangeRecord, TableBatch, ChangeBatch, EventKind Converters & Formats EventConverter, ConnectEventConverter, JsonEventConverter, EventFormat Consumer Base Class SchemaAwareChangeHandler

docs.title: End-to-End Conversion Pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Engine["Debezium Embedded Engine (JVM / JPype)"]
        DB[("Source Database")] -->|"CDC Stream"| DE["DebeziumEngine"]
    end

    DE -->|"list[ChangeEvent]"| HB["SchemaAwareChangeHandler.handle_batch()"]

    subgraph ConverterLayer["EventConverter Layer"]
        HB --> EC["EventConverter.convert(records)"]
        EC -->|"EventFormat.CONNECT"| CEC["ConnectEventConverter\n(Java SourceRecord + Connect Schema)"]
        EC -->|"EventFormat.JSON\nschemas_enabled=True"| JEC["JsonEventConverter\n(JSON {schema, payload} Envelope)"]
    end

    CEC & JEC -->|"Single-Pass Conversion\n+ Cached TableSchema"| CB["ChangeBatch\n(tuple[ChangeRecord, ...])"]

    subgraph Dispatch["Batch Sub-Grouping & Schema Tracking"]
        CB -->|"batch.to_table_batches()"| TB["Homogeneous TableBatch Runs\n(per destination & schema)"]
        TB -->|"reconcile_schema()"| CHECK{"Tracked Schema\nfor Destination?"}
        CHECK -->|"First Time Seen"| OTC["on_table_created(new_schema)"]
        CHECK -->|"new_schema != old_schema"| OSE["on_schema_evolved(new_schema, old_schema, diff)"]
        CHECK -->|"Unchanged"| HTB["handle_table_batch(table_batch)"]
        OTC --> HTB
        OSE --> HTB
        CB -.->|"Optional in handle_change_batch():\nof_kind() / group_by_kind()"| LIFE["Custom Batch Handling\n(TOMBSTONE / SCHEMA_CHANGE / HEARTBEAT)"]
    end

    HTB --> SINK[("Target Sink\n(Snowflake, Iceberg, Parquet, DuckDB)")]

docs.title: Deterministic Converter Resolution
docs.text:
At initialization, DebeziumEngine normalizes connector properties and format into a DebeziumConfig instance and configures the attached handler via handler.configure(config=self.config). SchemaAwareChangeHandler delegates to EventConverter.from_config(config=config) to instantiate the matching converter deterministically:

Converter Class Resolution Condition Execution Behavior ConnectEventConverter format="connect" (EventFormat.CONNECT) Consumes in-memory Java Kafka Connect SourceRecord objects. Compiles valueSchema() and keySchema() once per destination and converts records in a single pass via convert() / convert_event(). JsonEventConverter format="json" and schemas_enabled=True (default) Consumes JSON records containing explicit {"schema": ..., "payload": ...} envelopes. Compiles embedded schemas once per destination and converts payloads in a single pass via convert() / convert_event().

If format="json" is configured with schemas_enabled=False (or converter.schemas.enable=false), EventConverter.from_config() raises ValueError immediately rather than falling back to schema inference.

docs.title: Default Debezium Envelopes vs. Flat Rows (ExtractNewRecordState)
docs.text:
pydbzengine.schema is strictly pass-through with respect to payload shape: TableSchema.arrow_schema compiles the exact top-level struct emitted by Debezium, and ChangeRecord.value holds the converted dictionary matching that schema.

  • Default Debezium Envelope (no SMT): Debezium emits records with top-level before, after, source, op, ts_ms, and transaction fields. before and after are compiled as nested Arrow struct columns. Both SchemaDiff (is_additive, is_compatible) and TableBatch.to_arrow(target_schema=...) understand nested struct evolution when source table columns are added or widened inside before/after.
  • Flat Table Rows (ExtractNewRecordState SMT): When you want flat table columns directly in schema.arrow_schema and batch.to_arrow() (for example, when loading into a relational warehouse or lakehouse table), configure Debezium's io.debezium.transforms.ExtractNewRecordState transform with add.fields (such as op) and delete.tombstone.handling.mode (rewrite or drop). Each ChangeRecord.value is then a flat row dictionary with the table columns and any configured metadata fields at top level.

docs.title: Schema Compilation & Caching
docs.text:
When ConnectEventConverter or JsonEventConverter encounters a destination for the first time—or observes an updated wire schema—it compiles the schema in a single pass:

flowchart LR
    WIRE["Wire Schema
(Java Connect Schema or JSON dict)"] --> COMP["Schema Compilation
& Arrow Type Mapping"]
    COMP --> DEC["Compiled pa.Schema +
Value & Key Decoders"]
    DEC --> TS["TableSchema
(Cached per Destination)"]
  1. Schema Inspection: Reads each field's Connect wire type, Debezium logical type name, nullability, doc, and parameters.
  2. Arrow Mapping & Decoder Binding: Maps primitive, temporal, decimal, and nested container types to pyarrow.Field descriptors (preserving doc and debezium.logical_type in Arrow field metadata) and compiles format-specific value decoders.
  3. Destination Caching: Builds an immutable TableSchema (destination, arrow_schema, key_fields, key_schema) cached per destination alongside its decoders. Subsequent events with an equal wire schema reuse the cached entry without recompiling, and tombstones never evict active table schemas.

docs.title: Schema-Aware Consumer & Examples
docs.text: SchemaAwareChangeHandler (pydbzengine.schema.consumer, re-exported from pydbzengine.schema) is the base class for schema-driven CDC consumers. It converts incoming ChangeEvent batches via EventConverter, tracks the active TableSchema per destination, and dispatches homogeneous TableBatch runs while letting consumers split ChangeBatch by EventKind or destination in handle_change_batch().

docs.title: Lifecycle Hooks & Dispatch Sequence
docs.text:
When DebeziumEngine passes a batch of ChangeEvent records to SchemaAwareChangeHandler.handle_batch(), the handler converts the batch into a ChangeBatch and passes it to handle_change_batch(batch). The default implementation iterates batch.to_table_batches() (grouping EventKind.DATA records per destination and splitting only when TableSchema changes—never fragmenting on tombstones) and invokes:

  1. reconcile_schema(self, schema: TableSchema) -> SchemaDiff | None Atomically updates tracked schema state for schema.destination, calling on_table_created or on_schema_evolved before recording the new schema. Also available to custom handle_change_batch() overrides.
  2. on_table_created(self, schema: TableSchema) -> None Called the first time a TableSchema is observed for a destination.
  3. on_schema_evolved(self, new_schema: TableSchema, old_schema: TableSchema, diff: SchemaDiff) -> None Called whenever a destination's TableSchema differs from its previously tracked version (diff.has_changes), passing the computed SchemaDiff.
  4. handle_table_batch(self, batch: TableBatch) -> None Called for each homogeneous TableBatch after on_table_created or on_schema_evolved has completed.

To handle non-data event groups (TOMBSTONE, SCHEMA_CHANGE, HEARTBEAT) or custom cross-table / causal ordering, override handle_change_batch(self, batch: ChangeBatch) and slice batch with batch.of_kind(...), batch.group_by_kind(), and batch.group_by_destination().

You can inspect tracked schemas via self.schemas (returns a copy of dict[str, TableSchema]) or self.get_schema(destination).

When attached to DebeziumEngine, the engine calls handler.configure(config) automatically. For standalone use or testing, pass config=DebeziumConfig(...) or converter=... to SchemaAwareChangeHandler(...), or call handler.configure(config) directly. Pass default_variable_scale (default 10) to customize the Arrow decimal scale for VariableScaleDecimal fields.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Engine as DebeziumEngine
    participant Handler as SchemaAwareChangeHandler
    participant Conv as EventConverter
    participant Sink as Custom Consumer

    Note over Engine,Sink: Batch 1: Initial Records (v1 Schema: id, amount)
    Engine->>Handler: handle_batch([event_1, event_2])
    Handler->>Conv: converter.convert(records)
    Conv-->>Handler: ChangeBatch -> to_table_batches() = [TableBatch(dest="public.orders", schema=v1)]
    Handler->>Sink: on_table_created(schema=v1)
    Sink-->>Handler: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2))
    Handler->>Sink: handle_table_batch(TableBatch[v1])
    Sink-->>Handler: Load 2 rows via batch.to_arrow()

    Note over Engine,Sink: Batch 2: Upstream ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR
    Engine->>Handler: handle_batch([event_3_v1, event_4_v2])
    Handler->>Conv: converter.convert(records)
    Note right of Conv: Intra-batch evolution sliced into 2 homogeneous TableBatches
    Conv-->>Handler: ChangeBatch -> to_table_batches() = [TableBatch(v1), TableBatch(v2)]

    Handler->>Sink: handle_table_batch(TableBatch[v1])
    Sink-->>Handler: Load event_3 (v1 schema)

    Handler->>Handler: diff = v2.diff_from(v1)
    Handler->>Sink: on_schema_evolved(new_schema=v2, old_schema=v1, diff=diff)
    Sink-->>Handler: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR
    Handler->>Sink: handle_table_batch(TableBatch[v2])
    Sink-->>Handler: Load event_4 (v2 schema)

docs.title: PyArrow Consumer Example (Default Debezium Envelope)
docs.text:
Without an unwrapping SMT, Debezium emits standard CDC envelopes (before, after, source, op, ts_ms). TableSchema.arrow_schema compiles the envelope directly, and SchemaDiff.is_additive detects nullable column additions inside the nested before/after structs:

from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.schema import (
    SchemaAwareChangeHandler,
    SchemaDiff,
    TableBatch,
    TableSchema,
)


class ArrowBatchHandler(SchemaAwareChangeHandler):
    def on_table_created(self, schema: TableSchema) -> None:
        self.logger.info(
            "Table created: %s (key_fields=%s, columns=%s)",
            schema.destination,
            schema.key_fields,
            schema.arrow_schema.names,
        )

    def on_schema_evolved(
        self,
        new_schema: TableSchema,
        old_schema: TableSchema,
        diff: SchemaDiff,
    ) -> None:
        self.logger.info(
            "Schema evolved for %s: additive=%s, compatible=%s, added=%s, changed=%s",
            new_schema.destination,
            diff.is_additive,
            diff.is_compatible,
            [f.name for f in diff.added_fields],
            [old_f.name for old_f, _ in diff.changed_fields],
        )

    def handle_table_batch(self, batch: TableBatch) -> None:
        arrow_table = batch.to_arrow()
        self.logger.info(
            "Consumed %d records for %s (columns=%s)",
            arrow_table.num_rows,
            batch.destination,
            arrow_table.column_names,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    props = {
        "name": "arrow-cdc-consumer",
        "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
        "database.hostname": "localhost",
        "database.port": "5432",
        "database.user": "postgres",
        "database.password": "postgres",
        "database.dbname": "inventory",
        "topic.prefix": "cdc",
        "offset.storage": "org.apache.kafka.connect.storage.FileOffsetBackingStore",
        "offset.storage.file.filename": "/tmp/offsets.dat",
    }

    handler = ArrowBatchHandler()
    engine = DebeziumEngine(properties=props, handler=handler)
    engine.run()

docs.title: DuckDB / Arrow Sink Example (ExtractNewRecordState)
docs.text:
When loading into an analytical or relational table, configure Debezium's ExtractNewRecordState SMT (io.debezium.transforms.ExtractNewRecordState) with add.fields = op and delete.tombstone.handling.mode = rewrite. Debezium then emits flat table rows so TableBatch can be queried directly via DuckDB's Arrow PyCapsule support:

import duckdb
import pyarrow as pa

from pydbzengine import DebeziumEngine
from pydbzengine.schema import (
    SchemaAwareChangeHandler,
    SchemaDiff,
    TableBatch,
    TableSchema,
)


class DuckDBChangeHandler(SchemaAwareChangeHandler):
    def __init__(self, conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.conn = conn

    def on_table_created(self, schema: TableSchema) -> None:
        empty = schema.arrow_schema.empty_table()
        self.conn.execute(
            f'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "{schema.table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM empty'
        )

    def on_schema_evolved(
        self,
        new_schema: TableSchema,
        old_schema: TableSchema,
        diff: SchemaDiff,
    ) -> None:
        if not diff.is_compatible:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Incompatible schema change on {new_schema.destination}: "
                f"removed={[f.name for f in diff.removed_fields]}"
            )
        for field in diff.added_fields:
            col_empty = pa.schema([field]).empty_table()
            col_type = self.conn.execute(
                "SELECT column_type FROM (DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM col_empty)"
            ).fetchone()[0]
            self.conn.execute(
                f'ALTER TABLE "{new_schema.table_name}" ADD COLUMN "{field.name}" {col_type}'
            )

    def handle_table_batch(self, batch: TableBatch) -> None:
        # TableBatch implements __arrow_c_stream__, so DuckDB reads it directly.
        self.conn.execute(
            f'INSERT INTO "{batch.schema.table_name}" BY NAME SELECT * FROM batch'
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    conn = duckdb.connect("cdc.duckdb")
    dbz_props = {
        "name": "duckdb-cdc-engine",
        "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
        "database.hostname": "localhost",
        "database.port": "5432",
        "database.user": "postgres",
        "database.password": "postgres",
        "database.dbname": "inventory",
        "topic.prefix": "cdc",
        "table.include.list": "public.customers,public.orders",
        "offset.storage": "org.apache.kafka.connect.storage.FileOffsetBackingStore",
        "offset.storage.file.filename": "/tmp/duckdb_offsets.dat",
        "transforms": "unwrap",
        "transforms.unwrap.type": "io.debezium.transforms.ExtractNewRecordState",
        "transforms.unwrap.add.fields": "op",
        "transforms.unwrap.delete.tombstone.handling.mode": "rewrite",
    }

    engine = DebeziumEngine(
        properties=dbz_props,
        handler=DuckDBChangeHandler(conn=conn),
        format="connect",
    )
    engine.run()

docs.title: Lifecycle Events, Schema Alignment & Standalone Conversion
Handling Tombstones, DDL Events, and Heartbeats in Batch
docs.text:
Override handle_change_batch(self, batch: ChangeBatch) to split the batch via batch.group_by_kind(), batch.of_kind(...), and batch.group_by_destination() and process each group in batch fashion (while reusing super().handle_change_batch(batch) or self.reconcile_schema(...) for schema tracking):

from pydbzengine.schema import (
    ChangeBatch,
    EventKind,
    SchemaAwareChangeHandler,
    TableBatch,
)


class LifecycleAwareHandler(SchemaAwareChangeHandler):
    def handle_change_batch(self, batch: ChangeBatch) -> None:
        groups = batch.group_by_kind()

        if ddls := groups.get(EventKind.SCHEMA_CHANGE):
            self.logger.info("Received %d DDL event(s)", len(ddls))

        if data := groups.get(EventKind.DATA):
            for table_batch in data.to_table_batches():
                self.reconcile_schema(table_batch.schema)
                self.handle_table_batch(table_batch)

        if tombstones := groups.get(EventKind.TOMBSTONE):
            for dest, dest_ts in tombstones.group_by_destination().items():
                keys = [r.key for r in dest_ts]
                self.logger.info("Batch delete %d key(s) on %s", len(keys), dest)

        if heartbeats := groups.get(EventKind.HEARTBEAT):
            self.logger.debug("Latest heartbeat: %s", heartbeats.records[-1].value)

    def handle_table_batch(self, batch: TableBatch) -> None:
        table = batch.to_arrow()
        self.logger.info("Batch for %s: %d rows", batch.destination, table.num_rows)

For key-value sinks that require strict causal replay across interleaved DATA and TOMBSTONE events (for example, ExtractNewRecordState with delete.tombstone.handling.mode=tombstone), pass multiple kinds to of_kind() to preserve exact arrival order:

class CausalKvHandler(SchemaAwareChangeHandler):
    def handle_change_batch(self, batch: ChangeBatch) -> None:
        mutations = batch.of_kind(EventKind.DATA, EventKind.TOMBSTONE)
        for dest, dest_batch in mutations.group_by_destination().items():
            for record in dest_batch:
                if record.kind is EventKind.DATA:
                    if record.schema is not None:
                        self.reconcile_schema(record.schema)
                    self.logger.info("Upsert %s key=%s", dest, record.key)
                else:
                    self.logger.info("Delete %s key=%s", dest, record.key)

docs.title: Aligning Batches to an Evolved target_schema
docs.text:
When writing heterogeneous historical batches into a single target table schema (including nested before/after envelope structs on pyarrow>=19.0.0), pass target_schema to TableBatch.to_arrow():

aligned_table = table_batch.to_arrow(target_schema=latest_table_schema.arrow_schema)

to_arrow(target_schema=...) projects and reorders top-level columns, casts widened types (including temporal units and nested struct subfield additions, drops, and widenings while preserving surviving subfield order on pyarrow>=19.0.0, or full subfield reordering on pyarrow>=21.0.0), fills missing nullable columns with nulls, and enforces target nullability constraints recursively.

docs.title: Standalone EventConverter Usage
docs.text:
EventConverter can also be used directly without subclassing SchemaAwareChangeHandler:

from pydbzengine import DebeziumConfig
from pydbzengine.schema import EventConverter, JsonEventConverter

# Direct instantiation for schema-enabled JSON records
converter = JsonEventConverter()
change_batch = converter.convert(raw_events)

for table_batch in change_batch.to_table_batches():
    arrow_table = table_batch.to_arrow()

# Or resolve deterministically from DebeziumConfig (CONNECT or JSON with schemas_enabled=True)
config = DebeziumConfig(properties=dbz_props, format="connect")
config_converter = EventConverter.from_config(config)

docs.title: Domain Models & Data Types
docs.text: This page documents the public domain entities in pydbzengine.schema.models (re-exported from pydbzengine.schema) and the Debezium-to-Arrow type mappings in pydbzengine.schema.types.

docs.title: TableSchema
docs.text:
Immutable compiled schema descriptor for a CDC destination:

Attribute / Method Type Description destination str Full destination identifier (e.g., "cdc_prod.inventory.orders"). Whitespace-trimmed and non-empty. arrow_schema pa.Schema Compiled PyArrow schema matching the exact top-level event value emitted by Debezium (envelope struct by default, or flat table columns when using ExtractNewRecordState). key_fields tuple[str, ...] Field names extracted from the event key schema (e.g., ("id",) for struct keys, ("key",) for scalar keys, or () for keyless / map-keyed tables). key_schema pa.Schema \| None Compiled PyArrow schema of the event key, if present (non-map keys). namespace tuple[str, ...] Dot-split destination prefix excluding table_name (e.g., ("cdc_prod", "inventory")). table_name str Table name extracted from the final dot-separated segment of destination (e.g., "orders"). diff_from(previous) SchemaDiff Computes the structural difference from previous (TableSchema or pa.Schema) to self.

docs.title: SchemaDiff
docs.text:
Structural comparison result between a previous and new TableSchema (or pa.Schema):

Attribute / Property Type Description added_fields tuple[pa.Field, ...] Top-level fields added in the new schema. removed_fields tuple[pa.Field, ...] Top-level fields present in the previous schema that were removed. changed_fields tuple[tuple[pa.Field, pa.Field], ...] (old_field, new_field) pairs whose pa.DataType or nullable flag changed. reordered bool True if the relative order of surviving top-level fields changed. key_fields_changed bool True if TableSchema.key_fields changed (always False when diffing against a raw pa.Schema). key_schema_changed bool True if TableSchema.key_schema changed (always False when diffing against a raw pa.Schema). has_changes bool True if any fields were added, removed, changed, reordered, or if key metadata changed. is_additive bool True when changes consist solely of new nullable fields (top-level or nested inside structs such as before/after), with no removals, reordering, or key changes. is_compatible bool True when no fields were removed, key metadata is unchanged, all new fields (top-level or nested) are nullable, no lossy promotions occur (int64/uint64/decimal to float), and PyArrow permissive schema unification matches the new schema (supports lossless widenings such as int32 -> int64, float32 -> float64, decimal/temporal widening, nullability widening, and reordering).

docs.title: ChangeRecord & EventKind
docs.text:
ChangeRecord represents a single converted CDC event:

Attribute Type Description destination str Destination topic or table identifier. value dict[str, Any] \| None Converted payload dictionary matching schema.arrow_schema, or None exclusively for EventKind.TOMBSTONE. key dict[str, Any] \| None Converted key dictionary (required and non-empty for EventKind.TOMBSTONE). schema TableSchema \| None Compiled TableSchema for the event, if available. partition int \| None Source partition number, if present. kind EventKind Event classification: DATA, HEARTBEAT, SCHEMA_CHANGE, or TOMBSTONE.

Each event is classified into one of four EventKind values:

  • EventKind.TOMBSTONE ("tombstone"): value is None (delete tombstone carrying only key).
  • EventKind.HEARTBEAT ("heartbeat"): Destination starts with heartbeat_prefix or wire schema ends with io.debezium.connector.common.Heartbeat.
  • EventKind.SCHEMA_CHANGE ("schema_change"): Wire schema ends with .SchemaChangeValue / .SchemaChangeKey, or payload contains Debezium DDL marker fields ({"ddl", "databaseName", "tableChanges"}).
  • EventKind.DATA ("data"): Standard table change record.

In default Debezium envelope mode, access fields directly on record.value (for example, record.value["op"], record.value["before"], record.value["after"], record.value["source"]). When ExtractNewRecordState is configured, record.value contains the unwrapped table columns (plus any configured metadata fields like record.value["__op"]) directly at the top level.

docs.title: TableBatch & ChangeBatch
docs.text:
• ChangeBatch: Holds records: tuple[ChangeRecord, ...] in arrival order (supports len(), bool(), and iteration).
  • batch.of_kind(kind: EventKind, *more: EventKind) -> ChangeBatch: Returns a sub-ChangeBatch containing only records matching the given EventKind(s) in arrival order.
  • batch.group_by_kind() -> dict[EventKind, ChangeBatch]: Partitions records in a single pass into non-empty sub-batches keyed by EventKind.
  • batch.group_by_destination() -> dict[str, ChangeBatch]: Groups records in a single pass into sub-batches keyed by destination, preserving arrival order (chains naturally with of_kind(), e.g., batch.of_kind(EventKind.TOMBSTONE).group_by_destination()).
  • batch.to_table_batches() -> tuple[TableBatch, ...]: Groups EventKind.DATA records per destination into homogeneous TableBatch runs, splitting a destination's batch only when its TableSchema changes within the batch (non-data records such as tombstones, DDLs, and heartbeats do not fragment DATA runs).
  • TableBatch: Groups consecutive EventKind.DATA records for one destination sharing a single TableSchema (supports len() and iteration).
  • batch.destination -> str: Shortcut for batch.schema.destination.
  • batch.rows -> list[dict[str, Any]]: Converted record.value dictionaries matching schema.arrow_schema.
  • batch.to_arrow(target_schema: pa.Schema | None = None) -> pa.Table: Materializes a pyarrow.Table from batch.rows using schema.arrow_schema. When target_schema is provided and differs from schema.arrow_schema, aligns/reorders columns, casts existing columns via PyArrow (including temporal unit scaling and nested struct evolution on before/after fields; subfield reordering requires pyarrow>=21.0.0), fills missing nullable target columns with nulls, and recursively validates target nullability.
  • batch.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=None): Implements the Arrow PyCapsule Interface for direct interop with Arrow-native engines without manual conversion:
import pyarrow as pa

# Pass TableBatch directly to any Arrow PyCapsule consumer:
arrow_table = pa.table(batch)
# duckdb.sql("SELECT * FROM batch")
# polars.from_arrow(batch)

docs.title: Debezium-to-Arrow Type Mappings (pydbzengine.schema.types)
docs.text:
EventConverter resolves Debezium and Kafka Connect schemas through pydbzengine.schema.types into pyarrow.Field descriptors (preserving doc and debezium.logical_type in field metadata) and binds format-specific decoders in connect.py or json.py:

Category Debezium / Connect Types & Logical Names Target PyArrow Type (pa.DataType) Python Runtime Value Boolean boolean pa.bool_() bool Integers int8, int16, int32, int64 (and int-backed logical types such as Year, MicroDuration, NanoDuration) pa.int8(), pa.int16(), pa.int32(), pa.int64() int Floats float / float32, double / float64 pa.float32(), pa.float64() float Strings string (and string-backed logical types such as Uuid, Json, Xml, Enum, EnumSet, Ltree, Interval) pa.string() str Binary bytes (and io.debezium.data.Bits) pa.binary() bytes Fixed Decimal org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Decimal pa.decimal128(precision, scale) decimal.Decimal Variable Decimal io.debezium.data.VariableScaleDecimal pa.decimal128(precision, scale) decimal.Decimal \| None Date org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Date, io.debezium.time.Date, io.debezium.time.IsoDate pa.date32() datetime.date \| int Time org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Time, io.debezium.time.Time (ms), MicroTime / IsoTime / ZonedTime (us), NanoTime (ns) pa.time32("ms"), pa.time64("us"), pa.time64("ns") datetime.time \| int Timestamp org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Timestamp, io.debezium.time.Timestamp (ms), MicroTimestamp / IsoTimestamp (us), NanoTimestamp (ns), ZonedTimestamp (us, tz="UTC") pa.timestamp(unit, tz=None \| "UTC") datetime.datetime \| int Struct struct (envelopes, nested records, and struct-backed logical types such as Geometry, Geography, Point, SparseDoubleVector) pa.struct([...]) dict[str, Any] Array array (lists and array-backed logical types such as FloatVector, DoubleVector) pa.list_(item_field) list[Any] Map map (maps and io.debezium.data.Hstore) pa.map_(key_field, value_field) dict[Any, Any]

Preserving Debezium Logical Type Metadata

Logical types whose wire representation already matches a standard primitive or nested container (such as io.debezium.data.Uuid, io.debezium.data.Json, io.debezium.data.geometry.Geometry, io.debezium.data.geometry.Point, io.debezium.data.vector.FloatVector, and io.debezium.data.Hstore) compile cleanly through the corresponding standard handler while preserving their full Debezium logical type name in pa.Field.metadata[b"debezium.logical_type"].

Decimal Precision & JSON Null-Default Parity

  • Fixed and variable decimals compile to pa.decimal128(precision, scale) (1 <= precision <= 38, 0 <= scale <= precision), matching Arrow/Iceberg lakehouse conventions. Higher-precision source columns (>38 digits) fail fast unless configured with decimal.handling.mode=string or double.
  • In "connect" mode, ConnectEventConverter reads struct fields via getWithoutDefault() so explicit NULLs on nullable columns with SQL DEFAULT clauses stay None. In "json" mode, Kafka Connect's JsonConverter defaults to replace.null.with.default=true; set "converter.replace.null.with.default": "false" if you want identical NULL preservation in JSON mode.
